display.purpose: The "Narrator" wordmark on the picker screen. Used exactly once.

headline.purpose: Bottom-sheet and status titles (Settings, Front matter detected, Finished).

title.purpose: Compact inline book/chapter title in the player header.

body.purpose: The page text currently being read aloud; the only user-resizable content.

label.purpose: Section micro-headers, eyebrows, and most pill/button text.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Reserved for elements that genuinely float above the layout: the play button, book covers, the install banner.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Color/opacity transitions on interactive press states (buttons, dropzone border).

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Progress bar fill and active-sentence color transitions.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions (Tailwind's default).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one confirmable action in any sheet (Skip selected, Continue, Close).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #818cf8; color: #0f0f0f; font: 600 0.875rem system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; padding: 12px 32px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; transition: opacity 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:active { opacity: 0.8; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The non-destructive alternative action (Keep all, Start over) and the font-size stepper.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: transparent; color: #e4e4e7; font: 600 0.875rem system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; padding: 12px 32px; border: 1px solid #2a2a2a; border-radius: 12px; transition: background-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { background: #242424; }

components.name: Ghost Icon Button
components.description: Every header/nav icon: close, prev/next page, settings gear, dismiss banner.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-ghost" aria-label="Close"><svg class="ds-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M10.5 19.5 3 12m0 0 7.5-7.5M3 12h18"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: none; border: none; padding: 12px; color: #90909a; transition: color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:active { color: #e4e4e7; } .ds-btn-ghost .ds-icon { width: 20px; height: 20px; }

components.name: Segmented Pill Group
components.description: Every "pick one of N" decision in the app: playback speed, pitch, sleep timer, voice.
components.css: .ds-pill-group { display: flex; gap: 4px; } .ds-pill { flex: 1; padding: 8px 0; border: none; border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: #90909a; font: 500 0.75rem system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.1em; transition: background-color 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-pill:active { background: #242424; } .ds-pill--selected { background: #818cf8; color: #0f0f0f; }

components.name: Primary Transport Button
components.description: The single largest and most elevated control on screen — play/pause.
components.css: .ds-fab-play { width: 64px; height: 64px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #818cf8; border: none; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgb(0 0 0/0.1), 0 4px 6px -4px rgb(0 0 0/0.1); transition: background-color 0.15s; } .ds-fab-play:active { background: rgb(129 140 248 / 0.8); } .ds-fab-play .ds-icon { width: 28px; height: 28px; color: #0f0f0f; margin-left: 4px; }

components.name: Book Cover Card
components.description: Generated per-title gradient cover with progress track — the one place gradients and object-like shadow are allowed.
components.css: .ds-book-cover { position: relative; width: 128px; height: 176px; border-radius: 12px; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgb(0 0 0/0.1), 0 4px 6px -4px rgb(0 0 0/0.1); } .ds-book-cover__glyph { position: absolute; inset: 0; margin: auto; width: 40px; height: 40px; color: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.3); } .ds-book-cover__progress { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 4px; background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3); } .ds-book-cover__progress-fill { height: 100%; background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.7); }

components.name: Bottom Sheet
components.description: Every secondary decision — Settings, front-matter review, resume confirmation, completion — shares this exact chrome.

narrative.overview:
Narrator gets used in the dark, half-listening, at the end of a day — not stared at. The interface takes its cue from an instrument panel: near-black chrome, one signal color, every control sized for a thumb and a glance rather than a stare. But it stays intimate rather than clinical — this is a small warm light held in a dark room, not a piece of hardware. The explicit anti-reference is the corporate dashboard: no cool blue-on-white chrome, no data-density-for-its-own-sake, no sterile precision without warmth.

There is exactly one accent color, and it means one thing everywhere it appears: active, selected, or currently being spoken. Depth comes from three flat tonal layers, never gradients or blur — the single exception is book cover art, which is allowed to be decorative because it is the one place in the app meant to feel like an object rather than a control. Typography stays disciplined: the words being read are the only thing that gets visual size; every button, label, and header around them stays small and quiet.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black canvas with three discrete tonal steps of elevation, no gradients except book covers
One signal color (Soft Violet-Blue) marks everything active, selected, or speaking
System type only — no custom webfont, load-light and native-feeling by design
The bottom sheet is the only secondary-surface pattern; no centered modals, no extra routes
Reading content is the only thing that gets size; UI chrome stays at 12–14px

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Soft Violet-Blue is the only color in the entire system that communicates state. If something is accent-colored, it is telling you it's active, selected, or speaking — never decoration.

rules.name: The One Gradient Exception Rule
rules.body: Every surface in the app is a flat fill except book cover art, which is the sole place gradients appear — a generated per-title identity, not a decorative device.

rules.name: The Reading Priority Rule
rules.body: Only the page text currently being read renders at adjustable body size (14–24px). Every other piece of UI text — buttons, headers, labels, chrome — stays fixed at 12–14px, so the words being read remain the visual focus of the screen.

rules.name: The One Viewport Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one screen size to design for. The two unused breakpoint tokens are a reservation, not a signal to start building responsive layout.

rules.name: The Anchored vs. Floating Rule
rules.body: Anything docked to a screen edge gets a 1px border, never a shadow. Shadow is reserved for the small set of elements that genuinely float free of the layout.

dos: Do keep Soft Violet-Blue as the only color that means "active, selected, or speaking" — wherever it appears, it's marking state, not decorating.
Do use the bottom-sheet pattern for any new secondary surface.
Do keep interactive chrome (buttons, labels, section headers) at 12–14px; reserve size for the reading content itself.
Do respect env(safe-area-inset-bottom) on anything anchored to the bottom edge.
donts: Don't add a shadow to anything anchored to a screen edge — a hairline border is the correct treatment there.
Don't introduce a second accent color, or a gradient anywhere outside book cover art.
Don't add a custom webfont; the system-ui stack is a deliberate, load-light choice for an offline-first PWA.
Don't design for a breakpoint. This ships to one viewport: a portrait Android phone in an installed PWA shell.
